title: Double-Spend Race Condition in Escrow Release
problem: Two concurrent HTTP requests could trigger duplicate fund releases when buyer and seller confirmed delivery simultaneously. PostgreSQL row-level locks weren't sufficient because the ORM was reading stale state between transaction boundaries.
approach: Replaced optimistic locking with PostgreSQL advisory locks keyed to the escrow transaction ID. Wrapped the entire release flow in a serializable isolation level transaction. Added an idempotency key to the API endpoint to reject duplicate confirmations at the HTTP layer before hitting the database.
result: Zero double-spend incidents post-deploy. P99 latency for release endpoint increased by 12ms (acceptable trade-off for financial correctness). Added a regression test that fires 50 concurrent release requests against the same escrow ID.
file_content:
-- Problem: Concurrent escrow releases cause double-spend
-- Root Cause: ORM reads stale state between TX boundaries

-- Fix: Advisory lock + serializable isolation
BEGIN;
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;

SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(escrow_id);

UPDATE escrow_transactions
  SET status = 'RELEASED',
      released_at = NOW()
  WHERE id = $1
    AND status = 'PENDING';  -- guard clause

-- Idempotency: if status != PENDING, no rows affected
-- Application checks affected_rows == 1 before proceeding
COMMIT;

title: LLM Context Window Overflow in Data Extraction
problem: Local Mistral-7B model was silently truncating input when processing large PDF documents, causing incomplete data extraction. The tokenizer was counting tokens differently than the model's actual context window, leading to off-by-200 token errors on documents over 6000 tokens.
approach: Built a sliding-window chunking system with overlap. Each chunk is exactly 3800 tokens (leaving 200-token buffer for the system prompt and response). Chunks overlap by 15% to prevent entity splitting at boundaries. Added a post-processing merge step that deduplicates extracted entities using fuzzy string matching (Levenshtein distance < 3).
result: Extraction accuracy jumped from 72% to 94% on documents over 10 pages. Processing time increased linearly (expected) but total pipeline latency stayed under 8 seconds for a 30-page PDF on RTX 3060 hardware.

title: WebSocket Reconnection Storm on Deploy
problem: Every server restart during deployment caused all connected clients to simultaneously reconnect, creating a thundering herd that crashed the new instance within seconds. The default exponential backoff wasn't jittered, so all clients retried at identical intervals.
approach: Implemented a jittered exponential backoff with decorrelated randomization. Base delay starts at 500ms, doubles each attempt up to 30s max, with ±40% jitter. Added a server-side connection rate limiter (token bucket, 50 connections/second) that returns HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header when capacity is exceeded.
result: Reconnection storms eliminated. Deploy-time CPU spike dropped from 100% to 35%. Mean time to full reconnection for all clients went from 45s (with crashes) to 8s (smooth). Zero dropped connections in the last 3 months of deploys.
